subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw status treat live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth for external memory plugins, or is the current `not checked`/local-manager status behavior acceptable?
rationale: Current code mitigates the old wording but does not implement the requested live-runtime health signal, and the broader open issue plus conflicting fork PR need a maintainer-owned status boundary before automation can safely choose a fix.

options.title: Adopt the live-gateway status contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove both human and JSON status against a real external memory plugin without local startup side effects.

options.title: Accept current `not checked` behavior
options.body: Declare the shipped mitigation sufficient for status, close the conflicting fork PR, and only track broader plugin side-effect work separately.

recommendation.title: Adopt the live-gateway status contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger introduced the memory plugin runtime route and most recently reshaped the status scan behavior that controls this boundary.
